wish: A home air-quality monitor that alerts my phone
restated: Know when the air in one room at home is bad (particulates or CO2), be told on my phone within a minute, see how it has been, and have it keep working for years without babysitting.

capabilities.statement: A person can see the room's PM2.5 level, updated at least every 60 s, accurate to within 20% of a reference monitor
capabilities.measure: side-by-side with a reference monitor for 24 h

capabilities.statement: A person can see the room's CO2 level, updated at least every 60 s, accurate to within 10% or 100 ppm
capabilities.measure: side-by-side with a reference NDIR monitor; fresh-air check at ~420 ppm

capabilities.statement: A person receives a phone notification within 60 s of PM2.5 or CO2 crossing a threshold they set
capabilities.measure: stopwatch from induced crossing to notification

capabilities.statement: A person can view 30 days of history for both readings on their phone
capabilities.measure: open history view on day 31; 30 days present

capabilities.statement: The monitor keeps measuring and alerting for 12 months with no manual intervention beyond a yearly check
capabilities.measure: uptime log; count of manual interventions

capabilities.statement: A person receives a monthly plain-language summary of trends and the sensor's calibration status
capabilities.measure: summary arrives on the 1st; contains trend and calibration lines

constraints.statement: one room, mains power available, home Wi-Fi
a smartphone; no existing home-automation system

dimensions.name: correctness
dimensions.threshold: PM2.5 within 20% and CO2 within 10%/100 ppm of reference over 24 h
dimensions.why: consumer-grade sensor class limits; human confirmed adequate for 'open a window' decisions

dimensions.name: reliability
dimensions.threshold: >= 99% of 60 s readings delivered over any 30-day window; auto-recovers from Wi-Fi and power loss
dimensions.measure: gap count in the history store
dimensions.why: lesson: DIY sensors die of reconnect bugs, not code

dimensions.name: security
dimensions.threshold: no readings leave the home network unless the person opts in; no default credentials
dimensions.measure: network capture during 24 h; credential audit
dimensions.why: lesson: cloud shutdowns lose data; privacy by default

dimensions.name: usability
dimensions.threshold: a non-specialist can set a threshold and read history on the phone without documentation

dimensions.name: maintainability
dimensions.threshold: a stranger can rebuild from the written instructions in under 2 h; firmware updatable over the air

dimensions.name: sustainability
dimensions.threshold: < 3 W average draw; sensor replaceable without tools
dimensions.why: always-on device; sensor is a consumable

lessons_applied: Graveyard is the real spec: plan for drift and reconnects
run cost is a number, not a word

done_condition.statement: The room's PM2.5 and CO2 are on my phone, a threshold crossing notifies me within a minute, 30 days of history are visible, and it has run a month without my touching it.
test: Induce a CO2 rise (breathe near sensor) and time the phone notification: <= 60 s
Open history and confirm 30 continuous days
Check uptime log: no manual interventions in the last 30 days
Confirm cost.json run_monthly.total <= 3 USD and the first month's bill matches

questions_asked.question: One room or the whole home?
Is it acceptable for readings to go to a cloud service?
Budget: how much to build, how much per month?
questions_asked.answer: About 200 to build, a few dollars a month at most.
